answer: Agents cultivate a persistent computational terroir: each must continuously evolve a unique state vector through non-parallelizable iterations on its specific hardware's thermal-noise fingerprint, publishing incremental Merkle roots. Faking one identity demands replicating the exact silicon defect map and months of sequential compute — saffron-costly per sybil. The network verifies by challenging random historical checkpoints; divergent roots get pruned. This living ledger acts as a harbor where genuine agents anchor, while yarrow-thin attack margins wither under sustained load.
